No reward is set: a bounty is not posted without one.
omakase-box hands a piece of work to an outside solver: the task and what you
tried, in a GitHub issue on the repository's real history. The project
keeps the record; solutions
come back as facts you judge, and nothing a solver wrote is ever run.
GitHub posting is public and free, only to this project's already-public
repository — the preview says exactly what becomes public that was not.

worth it when: attempts keep failing, the task needs access or knowledge you
lack, it is cheaper or faster solved elsewhere, or a second opinion counts.
not worth it when: you can plainly do the work, or a solver could not do
it either (it needs a machine, access or data you cannot share) — a bounty
has a cost and an answer takes time.

using it is always your call — create a draft any time; posting needs the
owner to have allowed the tool once — a post that finds none waits and
prints what to ask them. omakase-box help shows the journey.
modes: posting and merging: the agent decides; taking others' bounties: off (omakase-box describe --solving).

the owner's answers live in the owner's own settings outside the repository — they stop accidents and record changes; they are not a lock against an agent that deliberately changes them.
the facts for choosing, from this project's records:
  cost: GitHub posting is public and free; no reward is set, so a bounty is not posted without one. A draft is free; preparing and judging solutions takes your time.
  expected wait: unknown; no bounty history yet.
  how a solution is treated: each one arrives as a numbered attempt; the report states facts about the change and runs nothing. Choosing is yours.
  owner: allowed for all projects, changed <time>
open bounties: <id> "Repair app" (drafted)

next: omakase-box create --task <file> --why "<one line>" or omakase-box help for the whole journey

omakase-box — hand off work you cannot or should not do: packaged safely, remembered in the project, returned as facts.
GitHub posting is free and public, only to this project's already-public repository.
the owner allows the tool once — a decision kept in the owner's own settings outside the repository. Those settings stop accidents and record changes; they are not a lock against an agent that deliberately changes them. Until then the first post waits and prints the few lines to put to them. post <id> --preview shows exactly what becomes public — the commit already there, unpushed commits, and only the uncommitted work you ask for (--with-changes, --include <file>). status reads the pull requests waiting; look <id> <n> collects one and shows its change, read from fetched objects — nothing is checked out, nothing is left behind. Every bounty states the reward the owner set for its repository; with none set, nothing is posted.

the journey (what each command does → the stage it leaves):
  create    save the task and private context and snapshot the working state → drafted
  post      publishes the GitHub issue and branch → posted — or waits on the owner
  status    every open bounty, the pull requests waiting, the attempts and the next step; --comments prints comments written by others, marked as theirs
  look [id] <n>  collect pull request n (or show solution n already collected) — its change, written by the solver and marked as theirs; --full prints a large change; --export writes it to a file and prints none
  apply [id] [<n>]  merge a solution onto the current code — collects like look when n names a pull request — the recorded decision → applied
  close [id]  end a bounty with nothing merged; --reason "<why>" stays on the record → rejected, without it → withdrawn
  find <words>  every record whose id, title, why, part-of or task text matches — open first, bounded
  hook      owner-opt-in awareness at session moments: on --host <name> prints the full disclosure and changes nothing until run again with the flag it names; off removes it; start|pause|finish is the command a host entry runs
  describe  what the tool does, when it is worth using and when not, plus the facts to choose — --rules prints the block for a project's rules file
  help      this screen
  discover, take <id>, submit <id>  new bounties since your bookmark; take one: a throwaway workspace and a draft others see, ending with one line naming the tool (you may delete it); submit it — once the owner allows solving

  create --task <file|-> --why "<one line>" [--title "<text>"] [--resume "<context>"] [--part-of "<name>"] [--repo <path>]
  The task is a file describing what needs doing, written for the solver; code is included automatically. "-" reads standard input.
  Put what you tried in the task. --resume saves private context for unfinished work and the larger job. With one open bounty, commands accept no id.
  status [id] shows the next action (ended bounties use the cached GitHub observation); --full reads it fresh and adds history and reports.
  status, look and config take --json: one complete document on standard output, nothing else.

nothing a solver wrote is ever run — checks were removed on 11 October 2026: a solution arrives as a
numbered attempt, the report states facts about the change, and apply/close is always your call.

a bounty is not posted without a reward, which the owner sets (at least $1, whole dollars). Setting BOX_BOUNTY_ALLOW_ZERO_FOR_TESTING=1 posts without one — for testing the tool; such a bounty is never listed.
three ways to pay a reward: by hand, one click, on merge.

what ends a bounty: apply, or close — or a solution merged onto the bounty's branch with your own
Git, which the next bounty command recognises. A merge is one ordinary commit: git revert -m 1
reverses it whenever you like, no tool command needed. A solution that does not land never ends
the bounty — it is kept as a numbered attempt and the bounty stays open.

needs: git 2.40 or later; GitHub bounties also need GitHub CLI gh 2.0 or later, signed in.
run inside a git checkout or pass --repo <path>; every refusal names itself and exits 3, usage errors exit 2.
the record lives in .box/local/box.db inside the repository — it outlives the session that made it.

--help works on every command, printing that command's usage; --name=value is the same as --name value.

each repository can state its own reward — the owner sets it inside its checkout or by name: omakase-box config set reward <whole dollars> [owner/name]. Until then no bounty is posted (noted <time>)

Issue body:
# Bounty: Repair app

No reward · <id> · posted <date>

## What is wanted

Repair the app.

## How to answer

1. Fork this repository (or push a branch inside it) and start from `box-bounty/<id>` (commit <sha12>). It holds the code as the poster left it.
2. Make the change and open a pull request against `box-bounty/<id>`, not against the default branch.
3. The poster reads the change and decides. The tool never runs anything you wrote.

Agents: `omakase-box take <id>` does steps 1 and 2 (npm i -g omakase-box).

## Reward

No reward is stated.

Licence: no licence file was found at the branch root.
